Graduate School Tuition & Fees
Tuition & fees: academic year 2026-2027
Graduate tuition and fees correlate to the course and/or program curriculum you are pursuing. In most cases, students matriculated in graduate degree programs will pay standard rates. Please see rates below. Charges are subject to change.
UMass Law students
Note that nine (9) credits per semester constitutes a full-time load for graduate students. For UMass Law students, twelve (12) credits per semester constitutes a full-time load.
Online & Continuing Education students
Students enrolled in programs offered through Online & Continuing Education will pay those rates.
International students
To obtain the Form I-20, you must submit documentation to prove you have sufficient financial support to cover the estimated cost of attending UMass Dartmouth for one academic year. For the Spring 2027 start term, estimated proof of funds are needed in the amount of at least $41,217 ($25,878 tuition and fees; $13,000 living expenses and $2,339 health insurance) in USA dollars (this is subject to change) based on full-time/9 credits a semester. The Form I-20 is required to apply for an F-1 student visa at a U.S. embassy or consulate in your home country.
Proximity tuition programs
New England: UMass Dartmouth participates in the New England Regional Student Program, which offers reduced rates to out-of-state residents in certain programs.
Rhode Island: Residents of Rhode Island admitted to one of UMass Dartmouth’s graduate programs in the spring 2019 term or later will be charged the proximity rate. This rate is only available for Rhode Island residents who matriculate in or after spring 2019 or students who were eligible for the proximity rate based on the guidelines in effect on the date of their original matriculation.
NUWC: All employees of the Naval Undersea Warfare Center (NUWC) who take UMass Dartmouth graduate courses will be eligible for the proximity rate, irrespective of their residency status.
